figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Design of a riboﬂavin-producing microbial cell factory with the GCR-DC strategy. The biosynthetic process of riboﬂavin from xylose
consisted of four modules. As module I was natively activated by xylose, a xylose-activatable pathway from Ru5P to riboﬂavin was constructed on a
plasmid to express the engineered modules II−IV under the control of xylose-inducible but glucose-insensitive promoters. As a result, the
engineered cells would preferentially use glucose for cell growth due to the presence of GCR and then utilized xylose for the biosynthesis of
riboﬂavin in a later stage. G6P, glucose-6-phosphate; F6P, fructose-6-phosphate; PEP, phosphoenol pyruvate; PYR, pyruvate; AcCoA, acetyl
coenzyme A; Ru5P, ribulose-5-phosphate; Xu5P, xylulose-5-phosphate; R5P, ribose-5-phosphate; PRPP, 5-phospho-α-D-ribosyl-1-pyrophosphate;
PRA, 5-phospho-α-D-ribosylamine; GTP, guanosine 5′-triphosphate; DRL, 6,7-dimethyl-8-ribityl-lumazine.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Time proﬁles of riboﬂavin production, carbon source consumption, and cell growth of DSM 2542 Rib-Gtg under diﬀerent cultivation
conditions. (A) Riboﬂavin productions of strains DSM 2542 and DSM 2542 Rib-Gtg in USYE medium supplemented with 2% xylose for 24 h. (B)
Time course of glucose and xylose consumption during the fermentation of DSM 2542 Rib-Gtg in USYE medium supplemented with 2% glucose
or 2% xylose, respectively. (C) Growth curves of DSM 2542 Rib-Gtg in USYE medium supplemented with 2% glucose or 2% xylose, respectively.
(D) Time course of riboﬂavin production during the fermentation of DSM 2542 Rib-Gtg in USYE medium supplemented with 2% glucose or 2%
xylose, respectively. (E) Time proﬁles of riboﬂavin production (orange), carbon source consumption (glucose, red; xylose, black), and cell growth
(blue) of DSM 2542 Rib-Gtg in USYE medium supplemented with 1% glucose + 1% xylose. Xyl, xylose; Glc, glucose. Error bars represent standard
deviations of three independent experiments. ***p < 0.001 relative to DSM 2542 strain (Student’s t-test).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Identiﬁcation of xylose-inducible and glucose-insensitive promoters. (A) Growth curves of G. thermoglucosidasius DSM 2542 cultured in
USYE medium with xylose and without xylose. The cells were collected at 4, 6, and 8 h for whole genome transcriptional analysis. (B) Number of
genes activated signiﬁcantly by xylose in DSM 2542. The Venn diagram indicates the number of genes activated by xylose according to the time-
series transcriptome analysis of DSM 2542 cultivated in diﬀerent conditions. (C) The strengths of the selected 39 putative xylose-inducible
promoters indicated by their reads per kilobase per million mapped reads (RPKM) values of downstream genes. (D) Promoter strengths measured
by GFP ﬂuorescence. The nine promoters showed little transcription without xylose and were labeled by asterisks. Strains were cultured in USYE
medium with or without 1% xylose. (E) Time courses of glucose consumption (red), xylose consumption (black), cell growth (blue), and GFP
ﬂuorescence (green) of strain DSM2542-RS11585 with the GFP reporter system driven by promoter P11585. DSM2542-RS11585 was cultured in
USYE medium containing 1% glucose + 1% xylose. (F) Dose-dependent activation of the promoter P11585 by diﬀerent concentrations of xylose
using ﬂow cytometry measurements. DSM2542-RS11585 was grown in USYE medium supplemented with a series of diﬀerent concentrations of
xylose as indicated. Error bars represented standard deviations of three independent experiments.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Decoupling the cell growth and riboﬂavin production in G. thermoglucosidasius DSM2542-DCrib by the GCR-DC strategy. (A) Schematic
representation of the rib cluster from DSM 2542 under the control of P11585. (B) Riboﬂavin production of DSM2542-DCrib in USYE medium with
2% xylose or 2% glucose for 24 h. (C) Transcriptional levels of genes ribD, ribE, ribA, ribH, and ribT in USYE medium containing 2% xylose or 2%
glucose. (D) Riboﬂavin production (orange), cell growth (OD600, blue), and carbon source utilization (glucose, red; xylose, black) of DSM2542-
DCrib cultured in USYE medium with 1% glucose + 1% xylose. (E) Transcriptional level of genes ribD, ribE, ribA, ribH, and ribT in USYE medium
containing 1% glucose + 1% xylose at the ﬁrst stage (at 5 h) and second stage (at 12 h), respectively. Error bars represent standard deviations of
three independent experiments. ***p < 0.001 relative to DSM 2542 strain cultured with glucose (Student’s t-test).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Reconstitution and optimization of the xylose-inducible
metabolic pathway from xylose to riboﬂavin. (A) Plasmids harboring
modules II, III, and IV controlled by diﬀerent combinations of
promoters. Totally, 27 diﬀerent plasmids were constructed. The prs
gene, 12 genes in pur operon, and the rib cluster were from modules
II, III, and IV, respectively. (B) Riboﬂavin production (orange bars)
and cell growth (OD600, blue symbols) of the 27 engineered strains. S:
strong promoter P11585; M: medium strength promoter P16610; W:
weak promoter P03225. Error bars represented standard deviations of
three independent experiments.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Eﬀects of the xylose/glucose ratios on riboﬂavin production and the production of riboﬂavin using the lignocellulosic carbon source. (A)
Evaluation of the inﬂuence of xylose/glucose ratios on riboﬂavin production of DSM2542-DCall-MSS. (B) Riboﬂavin productions of DSM 2542
Rib-Gtg, DSM2542-DCrib, and DSM2542-DCall-MSS using corn cob hydrolysate (Cch) as a carbon source. Strains were cultivated in USYE
medium with 0.5 and 1% corn cob hydrolysates for 24 h. (C) Time courses of glucose concentration (red), xylose concentration (black), biomass
(blue), and riboﬂavin accumulation (orange) of strain DSM2542-DCall-MSS in USYE medium with 0.5% corn cob hydrolysate. (D) Time courses
of glucose concentration (red), xylose concentration (black), biomass (blue), and riboﬂavin accumulation (orange) of strain DSM2542-DCall-MSS
in USYE medium with 1% corn cob hydrolysate. Error bars represented standard deviations of three independent experiments. ***p < 0.001
relative to DSM 2542 Rib-Gtg strain (Student’s t-test).
